current.name: ClipForge
current.summary: ClipForge has a new look: a space studio where a crew of 25 robots works on a cutaway ship, with what is being made beside it, Talk to AI always in the menu, a Brain map that flickers like lightning and your first clip in three steps.

changes.title: A space studio
changes.text: Every page has the new look: Courier Prime type under one starry sky, with a black hole over the Studio. Your projects, clips, accounts and settings are kept. If your accent colour was the old default violet, it becomes **Glacier** blue once; you can pick violet again in **Settings › Appearance**.

changes.title: The ship and its crew
changes.text: **Studio** is a cutaway ship with 25 robots and CORE. Every room is named, and the badge above each robot shows its job state (pick a robot to see its **Current task**). A team goes to its consoles only while it has real work (running, queued, waiting, or stopped by an error in the last half hour), and the work is handed on as the job really moves; a team with no work rests in the lounge. Under the ship: **Whole ship**, **Activity** (what the crew did for Autopilot, live streams and the Brain) and **Reduce motion**. **Bigger view** opens the ship on its own page.

changes.title: Working on, beside the ship
changes.text: Beside the ship, **Working on** shows what is being made now on a screen, with its current step and a light (Making, Your turn, Paused, Waiting or Ready; a live stream or a video you gave Autopilot shows Waiting there even while it is being made). Below it come what’s going on (the crew’s last three steps for Autopilot, live streams and the Brain), the queue, how many things need you (**Show me what** goes to the **Needs you** list under the ship), **Talk to ClipForge AI** and, at the bottom, **Next to publish** with a little picture of the clip and when it goes. The **Make** tab holds Make clips, Make a YouTube video, Make an animated short and Clip a live stream, the same four as **+ Make** at the top of every page. The Studio’s layout is new: a panel order saved in **Customize studio** no longer applies to it, and **Now making** and **Next to publish** always show.

changes.title: Talk to AI, always in the menu
changes.text: **Talk to AI** sits in the menu right under Studio on every page, and it is also a tab in the Brain. On a narrow window or a phone, the menu opens with **Menu**, which also has Autopilot.

changes.title: Your first clip in three steps
changes.text: **Make clips** reads 1 **Choose a video**, 2 **Pick what to make** (**Pick the best moments**, **Keep each story from start to finish** or **Split each story into Part 1, Part 2…**) and 3 **Make clips**, with working defaults. Style, example video, captions and framing, and uploading wait under **More options**. The project then says what it is doing, for example **Finding the best moments**, then **Rendering** while each clip is made, until **Your clips are ready**, and **Review clips** opens the clips. **Export** is now called **Save to computer**.

changes.title: The Brain as a galaxy
changes.text: **Brain › Memory** shows your **Knowledge map** as a galaxy with CORE in the middle. Each real link is a bolt of light in its collection’s colour that strikes again two to six times a second, at its own pace, and each note, style, skill and example video is a glowing ball. Picking one runs a light from CORE along its path and opens its details beside the map. **What ClipForge AI remembers** is Memory’s other view. The Brain’s tabs are Memory, Styles, Talk to AI, Agents and Decisions, with Example videos, Example notes, Skills and Performance history under **More**, and **Styles** has a caption preview you can play.

changes.title: Projects, Publishing, Accounts and Appearance
changes.text: **Projects** shows big cards with each video’s real length once it is known, then **Live recordings**: the live streams being recorded right now. **Publishing** has counts on its tabs, your time zone and the next scheduled post. **Accounts** shows your YouTube channel in a large card, a TikTok row with the next step it needs, and how sign-in tokens are protected. **Settings › Appearance** applies each choice at once, with a live preview of the Studio at desktop, tablet and phone sizes.

changes.title: As much motion as you like
changes.text: **Reduce motion** under the ship is the same switch as **Motion** in **Settings › Appearance**, and it follows your computer when it asks for less motion. With it on, the ship and the Brain’s lightning hold still; real work still shows. **Robot activity** there chooses **Full**, **Calm** (no breaks, games or snacks) or **Low power** (the robots stay still and the ship is redrawn once a second). Both also rest while the window is hidden.

checked: 3,109 automatic checks with made-up test videos, stand-in accounts and stand-in AI answers, on this version’s exact code. The 31 checks that render real video and audio ran on GitHub’s Linux machine.

Studio, Brain › Memory and Styles, Talk to AI, Projects, Publishing, Accounts and Settings › Appearance were checked in a browser at desktop, laptop and phone sizes: no sideways scrolling. Studio, Make clips, Brain › Memory, Talk to AI and Publishing were also checked with larger text at laptop and phone sizes: nothing cut off. The steps to a first clip, from + Make to Review clips, were walked through with the mouse only and with the keyboard only; the upload and the clip making were simulated, so no video was processed. The robots’ badges and room names were measured at 36 window sizes so that no badge covers another. The lightning was checked to hold still with Reduce motion, Low power and a hidden window, and the ship with Reduce motion and a hidden window.
This page’s notes and the Mac notes were checked claim by claim against this version’s code by four checkers and a skeptic for each, and what was wrong was corrected before release.
The Mac app was built, opened and tested with its own video tools, Keychain and window on an Apple-silicon Mac with macOS 15 in GitHub’s test service. The DMG on this page is that exact build.

The Windows setup was installed in GitHub’s test service over the previous version: it kept the same data folder and settings, opened the app, and closed and reopened cleanly. Every installed file was compared with the exact source.
not_checked: How smoothly the ship and the Brain’s lightning run on your own computer and graphics card. They were measured in a browser in the cloud, where one frame of the lightning took about 3 milliseconds.
The new look inside the Mac app’s own window and on a Windows PC; the screens were checked in Chromium on Linux.
Your own videos going through ClipForge while the robots work, and your real connected accounts on the new Accounts page.
Whether Windows security accepts the setup without asking. If it reports a threat, stop and read what it found; do not turn protection off.
Apple’s notarization. macOS will ask once before opening the app.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: Live clips put quality over quantity with a split view for face cams, you choose which channels each post goes to, and ClipForge AI uses your Brain to pick fuller clips and write post text your way.

changes.title: Live clips: quality over quantity
changes.text: When you add a stream in **Missions › Live streams**, **How picky** chooses how many clips it makes while the stream is live. **Only the best moments** (the default) listens for six minutes first, then makes about three clips an hour: each has to beat most of the stream so far, ClipForge waits two minutes after a strong moment ends in case a better one follows, and a standout moment can add one more. **Balanced** makes about six an hour, each above the stream’s average, and **Every good moment** works as before, a clip for every moment that passes the minimum quality. When the stream ends, the check of the full recording can still add clips until the stream has about three per recorded hour, or your **Clips per source** (5 unless you changed it) if that is more. Live clips now keep a moment’s build-up and ending instead of only its strongest few seconds. The stream’s card says why no clip was made when it passes over a moment. **Settings › Advanced** holds the starting choices for new streams.

changes.title: Stop clipping
changes.text: A live stream’s row has **Stop clipping**: ClipForge stops recording that stream and makes no more clips from it, neither now nor from the full recording. The clips already made stay, and with **Make & upload clips** they still go through the final checks and upload at their planned times. It cannot be undone for that stream. If you added a channel’s page (for example `twitch.tv/name` or `youtube.com/@name/live`) or a stream address, add the link again to clip its stream from then on; a link to one YouTube live video cannot be added again.

changes.title: Split view for videos with a face cam
changes.text: When a stream or gameplay video has a face cam over the picture, its clips now show the face cam across the top and the whole picture below it, with the captions on the line between. **Settings › Defaults › Split view** turns this off for new clips of the videos you add, and **Under the face cam** chooses **Whole picture** (the default) or **Zoomed in**. A live stream follows its own **Split view** choice, made when you add it; new streams start with **Settings › Advanced › Live streams: split view**. The clip editor’s **Layout** offers **Split view** and **Split if face cam** for one clip. A layout you chose for a video or clip always wins, and clips made before the update keep their look when you re-render them.

changes.title: Choose which channels each post goes to
changes.text: Every connected YouTube channel and TikTok account is listed with a tick box, and **All** for a platform with two or more. On **Prepare post**, a clip uploads to each ticked account, one after another. **Post selected…** on a video’s page sends several clips at once to the ticked YouTube channels, each with its saved post text, and leaves out a clip a channel already has unless you tick **Post them there again**; TikTok posts stay on Prepare post. In **Missions**, you tick the YouTube channels for each video or live stream you add. **Accounts › Tick for new posts** decides which accounts start ticked. With **Make & upload clips**, Autopilot plans one post per ticked channel, each approved on its own (automatically when it passes the final checks) with its own daily limit, posting gap and Reconnect notice, so a channel that needs Reconnect holds only its own posts.

changes.title: Share clips between channels
changes.text: With two or more YouTube channels ticked for a video or stream in Missions, **How the clips are shared between these channels** offers **Every channel gets every clip** or taking turns: each clip goes to one channel only, and the channels take turns so they get about the same number. A clip never moves to another channel once it has one.

changes.title: A smarter ClipForge AI in chat
changes.text: The chat now reads sixteen built-in playbooks (new ones for titles, post text and hashtags, and gaming and stream clips), a guide to ClipForge itself that says where everything is and links the page, and the advice of the skills you switched on in **Brain › Skills**. It answers questions like “how do I clip a live stream?” even without an AI model, and says what it read. With a model it can also look up a clip’s words and score and your settings.

changes.title: Clip picking follows your Brain
changes.text: Your memories, imported lessons, viral examples and the advice of your skills are read into the kinds of moment to look for or pass over (funny moments, big reactions, stories, small talk, ad reads and more). They move a clip’s score by about 8 points out of 100 at most (about 4 for one kind of moment), so they mostly change the order of close calls; a moment just under your **Minimum Viral Potential** can be lifted over it, and one just over it can drop under. A length you told it (“clips at least 40 seconds”) sets the lengths for that run. Click a clip’s picture on its video’s page to see what your Brain changed, and **Brain › Memory** counts each use.

changes.title: Longer, fuller clips
changes.text: The default clip lengths are now 25, 45 and 90 seconds for the shortest, ideal and longest clip. If your settings still had the old 15, 30 and 60 seconds, they change to the new lengths once; if you had changed any of the three, your lengths stay as they are. A moment’s strongest lines now come with their build-up and ending while the talk stays on the subject, never across a change of subject or a pause of more than three seconds.

changes.title: Lessons from your results
changes.text: When enough of your posted clips are at least two days old and have at least 10 views, the learning job compares clips that showed a kind of moment with clips that did not. It learns from TikTok’s numbers and from numbers you add in **Brain › Performance history** (**Add feedback / import**); YouTube’s own numbers count only if Google approved your project for it (**Settings › Advanced › Google approved derived metrics**). A clear difference, across several clips and videos on each side, becomes a memory such as “From your results: look for …” that clip picking and the chat read. Forget it and it stays forgotten; switch it off or rewrite it and ClipForge leaves it alone.

changes.title: Titles, post text and hashtags your way
changes.text: What you told ClipForge AI about post text is followed in every title and description it writes. Letter case, no emoji, how many hashtags and no call to action are always applied. For title length and a question as the title, it picks one of the clip’s own lines that fits, when there is one. It never adds words that were not said in the clip. Hashtags that say nothing about the video, such as #fyp and #viral, are dropped, and a clip gets five at most.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: The cloud computer for pictures and video now has its own place in Settings, so it is easy to find.

changes.title: Settings › Cloud computer
changes.text: The cloud computer you can rent by the hour to make pictures and video clips (added in 2026.11.13.2) now has its own entry in the Settings list. Open **Settings › Cloud computer** and press **Use a cloud computer** to see the box for your cloud computer’s web address and the step-by-step RunPod guide. **Settings › Pictures, video, voice** points to it too, and messages about the cloud computer now name it. Nothing else changed.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: Clip live streams while they are live, several at once, and let Make & upload clips post the best moments to YouTube during the stream.

changes.title: Clip live streams while they are live
changes.text: **Missions › Live streams** (also **Make › Clip a live stream**) takes the links of the streams you want to clip, one per line and up to 10 at a time: a Twitch or Kick channel, a YouTube live video or a channel’s live page (`youtube.com/@name/live`), or a public `.m3u8` stream address. ClipForge records each stream on your computer in one-minute pieces while it is live, without signing in or using your browser’s cookies, and turns strong moments from the last 15 minutes into vertical, captioned clips as the stream goes on. A channel that is not live yet is checked again until it starts, for up to a day. When the stream ends, ClipForge joins the whole recording and looks through it once more. It adds moments the live pass missed only up to **Clips per source** (Settings › Advanced, 5 unless you changed it), counting the live clips, so a stream that already made that many live clips usually gets none added.

changes.title: Long streams: raise Largest source first
changes.text: A recording stops when it reaches the **Largest source** limits in Settings › Advanced (8 GB or 240 minutes unless you changed them; a 1080p stream can reach 8 GB in roughly three to four hours) and is then finished like an ended stream, shown as Stopped. To clip longer streams, raise both numbers first; each stream sets aside that much disk room before it starts recording. The Live streams page shows your current limits under the link box.

changes.title: Uploads during the stream
changes.text: Each stream link gets its own **Make & upload clips** choice, with the same YouTube account, audience and made-for-kids answer you would give for a video. Clips that pass the final checks upload while the stream is still live, at your posting pace: with the usual settings the first goes out as soon as it is ready and later ones at least **Minimum gap** apart (30 minutes unless you changed it), per YouTube account and shared by all your streams. A clip that is already uploading or uploaded is never swapped for a later cut. The choice covers that one broadcast only, never the channel’s later streams. With **Make clips** instead, the clips stay on your computer.

changes.title: Several streams at once
changes.text: Add several links together, or more while others are recording. Up to three streams are worked on at the same time. Their recorded minutes are turned into text one minute at a time, taking turns with each other (and with any other transcription), and more streams keep recording and wait for their turn. Before a stream starts recording, ClipForge sets aside disk room for the streams already recording, so two streams never both start on a disk with room for only one.

changes.title: Stop recording, and one broadcast per link
changes.text: Each stream’s card has **Stop recording**: ClipForge stops the recorder, joins what it has and finishes the stream as if it had ended. Uploads made so far, and live clips already approved for upload, stay as they are; another live clip may still be replaced by a clearly better cut of the same moment from the full recording. If a channel goes offline, ClipForge waits 5 minutes in case the connection only dropped; a new broadcast on the same channel is never added to the old recording. To clip the channel’s next stream, paste its link again. **Stop all jobs** pauses the recordings (nothing is recorded meanwhile) and **Resume** continues them.

changes.title: Fixed: Cancel and Stop all jobs while a job is running
changes.text: If you pressed **Cancel** or **Stop all jobs** while a job was running, and that job then paused to wait, scheduled another try or crashed, it could be left waiting (or retrying) with nothing to pick it up, and after Stop all jobs it did not continue after **Resume** either. It now ends canceled (after Stop all jobs: held, like the other work Stop all jobs stopped), and your own Cancel of a running job stays final even if Stop all jobs comes after it.

changes.title: The privacy page and Terms describe live streams
changes.text: The privacy page (inside the app and linked at the bottom of this page) now describes live streams: what is recorded and kept on your computer, and that clips upload only to the YouTube account you chose for that stream. The Terms and the legal home page now also mention live streams you add.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: Make pictures and video clips on a cloud computer you rent by the hour (for example on RunPod) instead of on your own computer, and the Terms, privacy and legal pages now describe the app as it is.

changes.title: Pictures and video clips on a rented cloud computer
changes.text: Making pictures and clips is slow on a laptop, even a fast Mac. Settings › **Pictures, video, voice** now has a fourth choice, **A cloud computer**: rent a computer with a big graphics card by the hour (for example a RunPod “pod” with an RTX 5090 or a cheaper RTX 4090 and a 100 GB disk, using RunPod’s ComfyUI template), paste its address and press **Save and check**. ClipForge says **Connected** and names the graphics card, or says in plain words what is wrong (the pod is off, still starting, terminated, or the address is for the wrong port). To put a model on it, press **Put it on your cloud computer**: ClipForge shows one command to copy into the pod’s terminal, and the pod downloads the model’s files itself and checks their exact size and fingerprint, so your own internet is not used. The animated-shorts maker then gets its pictures and clips from there. Your videos, your projects, the voice and ClipForge AI stay on your computer; what goes to the cloud computer is what a picture or clip is made from (the words describing it, and a picture to animate), and its ComfyUI keeps a copy of what it makes until you delete it there. Making things on your own computer is still the default. Step-by-step instructions are on the same Settings page.

changes.title: It costs money while it is on
changes.text: A rented computer is charged for every hour it is on, even when nobody uses it, so press **Stop** on the pod in RunPod when you finish. A stopped pod keeps its models and address for next time, and its disk still costs a little (RunPod charges about $0.20 per GB a month, so about $20 a month for 100 GB). **Terminate** stops all charges but deletes the models. Keep the pod’s address to yourself: anyone who has it can use your cloud computer while it is on. ClipForge treats it like a password and never shows it to other pages.

changes.title: Terms, privacy and legal pages brought up to date
changes.text: The Terms of Service, the privacy page and the legal home page (inside the app and linked at the bottom of this page) now describe ClipForge as it is today: it no longer searches the internet for videos, there is a Mac app, **Make & upload clips** uploads to YouTube without asking for each clip, Find media searches Openverse, Wikimedia Commons and Pexels, and the new cloud computer, what it receives, what it keeps and what it costs.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: ClipForge AI becomes a real assistant with helper agents; plan a YouTube video by talking it through; animated shorts, with pictures, clips and voice-overs made on your computer; story clips as full stories or parts; and deleting projects.

changes.title: ClipForge AI talks for real
changes.text: Both chats (on a YouTube video’s page, and Brain › **Talk to ClipForge AI**) are now a real conversation. ClipForge AI reads what was said so far, knows your projects, your memories and its editing know-how, and writes its answer as it goes (**Stop** keeps what it wrote). It can also find and open your projects, look through your memories, show a button that opens a page, remember what you tell it, and propose a change to a video’s cut. When it wants to rename a project, forget a memory or delete a project, it shows a card, and nothing happens until you press **OK, do it** (for a delete, **OK, delete it**). It talks whenever a model is set up: the free built-in model, or an AI helper you chose in Settings › ClipForge AI. Without one, the old rules still answer and the chat offers to download the built-in model with one press. With an online AI helper, each answer sends the conversation, the memories and know-how that fit it, your project names and the details of the projects it looks at to that service (never your files or their sound), and says so under the answer.

changes.title: Helper agents that work alongside it
changes.text: Brain › **Agents** holds specialists that work with ClipForge AI: eight ready-made ones (Researcher, Script writer, Hook and title writer, Editor, Critic, Sound and music advisor, Thumbnail planner, Growth coach) that you add with one press, or your own with **Make your own**, described in your own words (24 helpers at most). ClipForge AI hands them jobs, you talk to one directly with **@Name**, and the ones set to **Helps plan new videos** add a short note when you plan a new video. Helpers think with ClipForge AI’s model, so they need one set up. They look things up, write and suggest; they never change or delete what you have, and they cannot search the internet.

changes.title: One daily limit for online AI
changes.text: **AI requests a day** (Settings › Advanced) used to count only the editor’s change requests. It now counts every request ClipForge AI sends to an online AI service: the chats (one answer can take several), the helpers, video planning and the editor’s change requests. It keeps your number (40 unless you changed it), and 0 sends none. A model on your computer is never counted for the chats, the helpers or planning; the editor’s change requests to it still stop at this number. Making clips, FilmCraft’s finishing, Autopilot and an animated short’s script are not counted.

changes.title: Plan a YouTube video by talking it through
changes.text: **Make a YouTube video** now starts with your files and your idea: drop in your videos, pictures and sounds in the order they should play, tell ClipForge AI your idea in your own words, and choose **Ask me questions** or **Just do it** (it plans from what you said and starts editing right away). With questions you talk it through: ClipForge AI writes a plan you can read (the name, who it is for, the length, how it opens, the story in order, what to keep and cut, music, captions), asks a few short questions at a time with quick answers, and changes the plan as you talk or as you edit any line yourself. **Build my video** edits the video from the plan. The plan stays on the editor page, where changing it edits again as a new version. Once you start, the video waits in Projects (“Planning with ClipForge AI”) with your files, the conversation and the plan saved as you go. Without a model, the built-in rules read the plan from what you say.

changes.title: Delete projects
changes.text: Every card on the Projects page has a trash button. It opens a window that lists exactly what will be deleted for good and what stays, and nothing happens until you press **Delete project**. Deleting removes what ClipForge keeps only for that project: its clips or edit history, renders, its own copy of the video when nothing else uses it, its ClipForge AI chat and the notes kept only for it, and for an animated short the pictures and clips made for it. Its planned posts not yet sent are canceled (they stay in your post history). Your own files, media another project uses, anything already posted and what ClipForge AI learned for all videos stay. Work running on the project is stopped first; while Autopilot or a post is busy with it, or its video is still being copied in, the window says why it has to wait. On Windows, a file another program has open is removed the next time ClipForge starts.

changes.title: Pictures, video clips and voice-overs made on your computer
changes.text: ClipForge can make still pictures, short video clips (up to 5 seconds) and voice-overs itself, for free, and nothing goes online once the files are downloaded. Pictures and clips come from ComfyUI, a free program that ClipForge sets up for itself with one button (or the ComfyUI desktop app if you already have it), with three models: Z-Image Turbo and FLUX.2 klein for pictures and Wan 2.2 for clips. The voice (Supertonic 3, 10 voices, English for now) runs inside ClipForge. Settings › **Pictures, video, voice** recommends what suits your computer. These are big downloads: about 16 GB (FLUX.2 klein), 21 GB (Z-Image Turbo) or 23 GB (Wan 2.2) for a model and about 400 MB for the voice. Pictures run well on a Mac with 16 GB of memory or more, or an NVIDIA card with 8 GB or more, and a video clip takes minutes. Each model, the voice and ComfyUI itself are checked against an exact size and fingerprint. The voice and Wan 2.2 come with use rules you agree to before the download; the voice’s ask you to say that the voice is AI-generated where you post. For now the animated-shorts maker uses them, and Settings has a quick test for each.

changes.title: Animated shorts
changes.text: **Make › Make an animated short** makes the voice-over shorts seen on TikTok: choose **Paste my script**, or **Write it for me** with a topic, a tone and a length (this needs ClipForge AI; the free built-in model works). Each scene gets a voice, a picture and a gentle camera move (with the video maker set up, you can choose **Animate the pictures with the video maker** instead), with big captions where the spoken word lights up, music under the voice and a soft whoosh on every other cut. Every scene can be changed on its own afterwards (words, picture, camera move, order, add, delete), and the usual editor, preview, render and FilmCraft work on it. Without the picture and voice makers it still works, with your computer’s own voice and designed cards showing each scene’s key words. With an online AI helper chosen, the topic, or a pasted script for its picture ideas, is sent to it.

changes.title: Story clips: Full story or Story parts
changes.text: Every story clip now shows the whole picture, centred and still over a blurred copy, with the captions just above it when there is room, instead of following faces. It was made for videos where someone reads stories aloud over gameplay; to frame one video differently, use **Customize captions and framing** in Make clips. **Full story** makes one clip per story, and **Story parts** cuts each story that is long enough at its most gripping places into parts of about one to three minutes (Part 1, Part 2…). No new story clip is longer than five minutes: a longer story is split into parts. On 40 made-up test transcripts of someone reading four posts over gameplay, ClipForge now finds the 4 stories every time; before, it cut them into 9 to 21 clips.

changes.title: Fixed: files on other computers
changes.text: On Windows, a web page, or a FilmCraft project made to do it, could make ClipForge look at a file on another computer, which signs in to that computer as you. ClipForge now refuses such addresses from web pages and FilmCraft projects before looking at anything. Footage on a network drive with its own drive letter still works.

changes.title: Fixed: two uploads finishing at once
changes.text: Two uploads of the same file that finish at the same moment no longer fail.

changes.title: The privacy page says more
changes.text: The privacy page (linked at the bottom of this page, and inside the app) now also says what ClipForge AI’s chats, memories and helpers keep and send, what deleting a project removes, and what uploads, animated shorts and the picture, video and voice makers store, download and send.

windows.requires: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, with Python 3.12 and FFmpeg

previous.name: ClipForge
previous.summary: A far smarter ClipForge AI that understands meaning, reads the whole video, judges, looks and listens; long videos with full stories, big footage and your script; and a new look.

changes.title: ClipForge AI understands what is said
changes.text: A small meaning model (90 MB, downloaded once from a fixed source and checked against fixed fingerprints, running on your computer) can tell that two sentences say the same thing in different words. It helps pick clips that stay on one topic and tie their ending back to their opening, tells stories apart in long videos, and finds the brain memory that means what you asked. Settings › AI helper › **Understanding meaning** shows it, and everything still works without it.

changes.title: It reads the whole video and judges the finalists
changes.text: Before scoring, ClipForge AI reads the transcript from start to end and names moments the word lists miss (a story told plainly, a quiet confession, a joke in ordinary words); each one still has to pass every check. At the end it puts the finalists side by side and gives each a green, yellow or red verdict with a reason. Its ranking can move a Clip Score by at most 10 points, and a red verdict is shown as a warning. It never adds or removes a clip on its own.

changes.title: It looks at the picture and listens to the voice
changes.text: The built-in model now looks at frames of the strongest clips, rates how much the picture holds a viewer (at most 4 points), and picks the thumbnail. From the sound alone ClipForge measures emphasis (where the voice rises and strengthens), laughter and a flat delivery; a flat voice is named in the clip’s “Why”, and **Edit it for me** puts its punch-in zooms where your voice leans on a word (and on every other cut, as before, when your voice stays even).

changes.title: It learns your taste
changes.text: Every clip you untick, put back, export or publish is a lesson. After twelve (at least four kept and four left out), ClipForge AI adjusts new finalists by at most 6 points and says why (“you tend to keep clips with a stronger hook and leave out long ones”). Brain › Memory shows **What it learned from your choices** and can forget it.

changes.title: Every Clip Score explained
changes.text: The deeper analysis now runs for every Make clips, not only Autopilot, from a broader pool. Each clip shows what the scout said, the judge’s rank and verdict, what the AI saw, what the voice did, your taste, and **How the Clip Score came about** line by line. Three more rules from the research guides: clips whose beats turn on “but”, “because” or “which meant” score higher on curiosity, an “and then, and then” chain loses points and gets a warning, “I spent 30 days…” counts as a hook, and “furthermore” or “my next point” counts as a topic change.

changes.title: Full stories: one clip per story, no questions
changes.text: For a video of someone reading posts, Full stories learns the narrator’s own separators (“next story”, a post title read out, numbering), keeps updates and top comments with their story, runs every story to the next one, and makes each clip at once without asking you anything. With the meaning model it also catches a change of subject the words hide, and with a model set up it reads the recording through for a table of contents and names the stories.

changes.title: Big footage, used where it is
changes.text: On the desktop, **Add from this computer** browses your folders and uses files where they are: nothing is copied, and a folder of many gigabytes goes in. Long recordings are listened to in pieces that carry on after a restart, and previews come from a small copy while the final render always uses the original.

changes.title: Your script
changes.text: Drop, choose or paste a script (.txt, .md, .docx, .pdf, .fdx or plain text) on the Make a YouTube video page. Every spoken line is matched to the footage, the cleanest take of each line plays and the other takes wait a click away (**Use this take**), a heading is a chapter, and missing lines are named. The editor page gets a **Script** panel.

changes.title: A smarter Edit it for me
changes.text: Without a script, the cleanest take of a line said more than once plays and the rest are switched off in place, warm-ups and camera chatter are left out, a video of two minutes or more opens with its strongest line, and ClipForge AI reads the whole video inside a time budget instead of the first part only.

changes.title: A new look
changes.text: One design system for the whole app: layered dark surfaces lit from the top edge, sunken wells where media goes, lifted buttons, the footage the brightest thing on the page and one accent colour for the way forward. Settings is a side list of sections, loading pages show the shape of what is coming, and the four palettes and six accents in Customize studio were retuned.

previous.summary: ClipForge AI: a built-in model, a memory and a chat, editing know-how from two filmmaking guides, and FilmCraft inside the app.

changes.title: ClipForge AI knows how to edit
changes.text: Twelve built-in playbooks distilled from two filmmaking and short-form video guides: hooks and openings, endings, pacing, captions, voice and sound, music and colour by mood, effects, picking a clip, platforms, retention and talking heads. ClipForge AI reads the ones that fit when it answers you, proposes a change, edits for you or finishes in FilmCraft, and what you teach it always wins. Brain › Memory lists them under **What it knows about editing**, and Brain › Talk answers editing questions from them even without a model.

changes.title: Clips, hooks and captions follow the numbers
changes.text: Endings that announce the end (“to recap”, “thanks for watching”) rank lower, so the point before them wins; warnings and mistakes to avoid rank higher as hooks; the hook headline starts below the apps’ top bar and shrinks to fit; bottom captions now sit above the bar the phone apps draw over the video.

changes.title: Colours in rendered clips
changes.text: Fixed: clips were converted with the wrong colour matrix (BT.601), a visible shift of reds and greens in every clip. They are now converted and tagged the way phones and players expect (BT.709), with a keyframe every half second and 256 kbps sound.

changes.title: Talk to ClipForge AI
changes.text: Every video has a chat, and Brain › Talk is the general one. Say “remember: always keep my intro” and it keeps a rule (“for this video” keeps it to one video); ask “what do you know?”, “why?” or “forget that”. Brain › Memory shows what it remembers (rules, facts, what it did) with a health check, Tidy, export and import. The AI helper is now called ClipForge AI.

changes.title: A model that comes with the app
changes.text: Settings › ClipForge AI › **Built-in model** downloads a free model on first use (Basic, Standard or Pro), checked against a pinned hash: no key, no account, and nothing leaves your computer. A free key or a local Ollama or LM Studio model still works. With a model, ClipForge AI can advise the edit, answer anything in the chat and finish in FilmCraft.

changes.title: Clean up the sound
changes.text: One button cleans a noisy voice recording (a small noise model downloaded on first use) and polishes it with the dialogue chain: less rumble and mud, more presence and gentle compression.

changes.title: FilmCraft and EffectCraft inside ClipForge
changes.text: Final videos can be edited and rendered in FilmCraft, ArtCraft’s open-source editor, inside ClipForge (Settings › Editing apps): ClipForge AI finishes the edit with FilmCraft’s tools (looks, transitions, motion, titles) and with animated titles made in EffectCraft, rendered as shots and put into the final video, and **Edit version … in FilmCraft** opens the result in FilmCraft’s own editor page so you can keep working and save a new version. Both apps are downloaded on first use and checked against pinned hashes; the built-in editor stays as backup.

changes.title: Edit it for me
changes.text: ClipForge edits the video instead of only lining up your files: it cuts long pauses, lone “um”s and the first take of a line you said twice, and fits the length you ask for. Pictures appear over the video when you mention them, and free music and soft sound effects made on your computer are added. Every cut is listed, and anything left out can be put back. Pick **Fast-paced** for tighter cuts with punch-in zooms, or **Keep my clips as they are**.

changes.title: A free AI helper, if you want one
changes.text: ClipForge edits well on its own. To let an AI help choose what to cut and where pictures go, open **Settings › AI helper**: download a free model that runs on your computer (Ollama or LM Studio, or import a `.gguf` file you have), or paste a free key from Google Gemini, Groq or OpenRouter. It is sent the words said in your videos as text and your answers to the questions, never the video or the sound.

changes.title: YouTube links on the Mac
changes.text: Fixed: a YouTube link could end with “No downloadable video was found”. The Mac app now uses its built-in video tools to join YouTube’s picture and sound, and includes the helper YouTube needs.

changes.title: Video links
changes.text: Paste a link to one public video. ClipForge checks it as you type, downloads only that video, and never signs in or reads your browser’s cookies. For a private video, use your own file.

changes.title: The whole project in the editor
changes.text: No limit on the number of files. Each change is saved as a version you can name, undo or return to. Type what to change (“shorten the introduction”) and you see the exact edit before it is applied.

changes.title: Learn from an example video
changes.text: Add a video whose editing you like. ClipForge measures its cuts, pacing, captions and framing on your computer and keeps them as a style you can edit, use or turn off.

changes.title: Find media
changes.text: Search Openverse, Wikimedia Commons and Pexels for images, footage, music and sound effects from inside the editor. Each result shows its license, and unclear terms are labelled before you use them. Pexels needs your own free key.

changes.title: The Brain map
changes.text: Every style, skill, example video and note, and the projects that really used them. A line appears only where a project recorded using something; nothing is guessed.

changes.title: A dark studio, your way
changes.text: One calm dark design, a Customize studio panel, and the robot office inside the Studio. Rename any robot; its job stays the same.

changes.title: No more internet search
changes.text: ClipForge no longer searches the internet for videos to clip. It works only on the videos and links you add.

changes.title: A new name
changes.text: ClipFoundry is now ClipForge. The Mac app and the Windows file keep the ClipFoundry name so your Brain, accounts, clips and settings are found and kept.

changes.title: Full stories
changes.text: Besides **Highlights**, pick **Full stories** for one complete clip per story, from its setup to its ending. A story too long for an account is kept whole, and ClipForge tells you which accounts can take it.

changes.title: Make a YouTube video
changes.text: Drop in your clips and images, answer four short questions, and get a rough cut you can still change: move or remove clips, shorten the introduction, set captions, transitions and music level. Every change is a version you can go back to.

changes.title: Your style, saved
changes.text: Save a style once with **Remember this style**, or import a written editing skill. Every project shows exactly what it used from your Brain.

changes.title: Several accounts
changes.text: Connect more than one YouTube channel and TikTok account, and choose where each project goes. TikTok posts always wait for your OK.
